'''Frances Rosemary Balkwill''' {{post-nominals|OBE|FRS|FMedSci}} (born 1952) is an English scientist, Professor of Cancer Biology at [[Queen Mary University of London]], and author of children's books about scientific topics.

== Early life and education ==

Balkwill was born in south-west London in 1952, and was educated at [[Surbiton High School]]. She obtained a BSc in Cellular Pathology at the [[University of Bristol]] and a PhD on leukaemia cell biology<ref name=PhDf>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=Queen Mary, University of London|url=https://search.library.qmul.ac.uk/iii/encore/record/C__Rb1229260__SBalkwill,%20F.%20R.__Orightresult__X4|doi=|title=Investigations into the Nature of Human Acute Leukaemia Using Cell Culture Techniques|first= Frances Rosemary|last=Balkwill|date=1977|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.448740}}|website=qmul.ac.uk|oclc=500377266|hdl=}}</ref> in the Medical Oncology Department at [[St Bartholomew's Hospital]] supervised by [[Gordon Hamilton Fairley]].<ref name=":0">{{cite journal|last1=Watt|first1=Fiona|title=Women in Cell Science|publisher=The Company of Biologists|issue= Pt 7|date=1 April 2005|pmid=15788651|doi=10.1242/jcs.01688|volume=118|pages=1339–40|journal=Journal of Cell Science|doi-access=}}</ref>

== Career ==

She worked for several years at the ICRF Lincoln's Inn Fields (now [[Cancer Research UK]] London Research Institute)<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cancerresearchuk.org/our-research/researchers/professor-fran-balkwill | title=Professor Fran Balkwill | date=26 November 2015 }}</ref> on the effect of [[interferon]] on cancer. In 2000 she moved to [[Queen Mary, University of London]], where she is Professor of Cancer Biology and Director of the Centre for Translational Oncology in the Cancer Research UK Clinical Cancer Centre.<ref name=":0" />

In addition to her laboratory research, Balkwill has written many children's books about science, illustrated by Mic Rolph,<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.embo.org/news/press-releases/2004/uk-scientist-and-children-s-author-wins-embo-award-for-communications-2004|title=UK scientist and children's author wins EMBO Award for Communications 2004|work=EMBO|access-date=2018-10-18|language=en-gb|date=5 November 2004|archive-date=18 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181018201545/https://www.embo.org/news/press-releases/2004/uk-scientist-and-children-s-author-wins-embo-award-for-communications-2004|url-status=dead}}</ref> and is Director of Centre of the Cell, a science education centre for children in the new [[St Bartholomew's Hospital|Barts]] and The London Medical School building in [[Whitechapel]], east London.<ref name=":0" /> Her books for children cover a range of topics in biology. For her first book on [[HIV/AIDS|HIV and Aids]], ''Staying Alive: Fighting HIV/AIDS'' (2002), Balkwill and Rolph travelled to South Africa to carry out research and to determine the educational needs of local communities. 19,000 free copies of the book were distributed throughout South Africa, funded by the publisher [[Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory Press]].<ref name=":1" />

From 2008 to 2011, Balkwill served as Chairman of the Public Engagement Strategy Committee at the [[Wellcome Trust]]. In 2016 she was a judge for the [[Wellcome Book Prize]].<ref name=":2">{{Who's Who|id = U4000437|title=Balkwill, Prof. Frances Rosemary|author=Anon|year=2021|doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U4000437}}</ref>

=== Awards and honours===
In 2008 Balkwill was awarded an [[Order of the British Empire]] (OBE).<ref name=":2" />

Balkwill's books for children ''Cells are Us'' and ''Cell Wars'' won the [[Royal Society]] Young People Book Prize in 1991.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1nPKyiKYa2kgU06GjnUncd6Vq-wfBrG6n-6KR7PBjzP4/edit#gid=0|title=Young People Book Prize: All winners, shortlisted and longlisted|work=The Royal Society Young People’s Book Prize|access-date=2018-10-18|agency=Google Docs|language=en}}</ref>

She won the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO) Award for Communication in the Life Sciences in 2004.<ref name=":1" /> She was awarded the [[Michael Faraday Prize]] in 2005 "for her outstanding work in communicating the concepts, facts and fascination of science in a way that appeals to children of all ages, backgrounds and nationalities, while at the same time maintaining a distinguished research career".<ref>{{cite news |last=Fleming |first=Nic |title=Laws of attraction in action |publisher=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]] |location=England |date=31 January 2006 |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/technology/3344716/Laws-of-attraction-in-action.html}}</ref> In 2006 she was awarded [[Fellow of the Academy of Medical Sciences|Fellowship of the Academy of Medical Sciences]] (FMedSci) for her contributions to and achievements in medicine.<ref name=":2" />

In 2015 she received an Honorary degree from the University of Bristol.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://www.bristol.ac.uk/graduation/honorary-degrees/2015.html/balkwill.html|title=Professor Frances Balkwill, OBE|last=Bristol|first=University of|website=bristol.ac.uk|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-10-18}}</ref>

In 2017 she was awarded the Inspiring Leadership in Research Engagement Prize from [[Cancer Research UK]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bci.qmul.ac.uk/en/news/grants-a-awards/item/prof-fran-inspiring-leadership-in-research-engagement-prize|title=Prof. Fran Balkwill wins Inspiring Leadership in Research Engagement Prize|last=Leech|first=Zoe|website=bci.qmul.ac.uk|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-10-18 |url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181018163520/https://www.bci.qmul.ac.uk/en/news/grants-a-awards/item/prof-fran-inspiring-leadership-in-research-engagement-prize|archive-date=2018-10-18}}</ref>

In 2021 she received the Beetlestone Award, recognising her leadership and legacy in the field of informal science learning.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.qmul.ac.uk/media/news/2021/smd/queen-mary-academic-receives-prestigious-science-learning-award.html|title=SMD - Queen Mary academic receives prestigious science learning award - Queen Mary University of London|date=16 June 2021 }}</ref>

In 2024, she was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Outstanding scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2024/05/new-fellows-2024/ |access-date=2024-05-18 |website=Royal Society |language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==

Balkwill has two children, Jessica and Barnaby. She has 5 grandchildren Sabrina, Esme, Casper, Balthazar and Aurelius.<ref name=":3" />
